text:
笑死我了，bro 以为自己抓住了一个绝佳的机会，可以公开嘲讽 Codex负责人Tibo  ，结果一刀捅在了自己身上🤣

起因是 @thsottiaux  在回复一个用户：Sol 支持 1M Context，你还想要多大？

然后bro @ravikiran_dev7  直接截图嘲讽tibo：

你连自己产品都不知道！Codex 明明只有 272K！

问题是GPT-5.6 Sol 的API本来就支持 1M Context😅

272K 是你在 Codex 里看到的产品层/配置限制，不是 Sol 这个模型只能跑 272K。

也就是说他特意截了张图配上三个问号，发给十几万人看，想证明 OpenAI 高管不懂 GPT-5.6。

最后成功证明了自己没搞清楚「模型 Context Window」和「Codex 的 Context Window」是两回事。

你以为自己在 Fact Check 别人，

其实你才是那个 Fact。

这是今天最逗我乐的一条了🫡

增持
1. 亚马逊 $AMZN
最大仓位，$1.1亿。全球最大的云服务和数据中心运营商，AI算力爆发直接推高其电力需求，公司还积极布局小型核反应堆，能长期吃到AI能源红利。

2. Vista Energy $VIST
阿根廷Vaca Muerta页岩油区的主力生产商，产量持续快速增长，受益于全球能源需求和当地政策支持，成长性突出。

3. Vistra $VST
拥有大量核电和天然气发电资产的独立电力商，正好卡住AI数据中心最缺的稳定电力供应，是典型的“卖铲人”标的。

4. 美国电力 $AEP
大型受监管公用事业公司，电网和输电项目多，能稳定分享AI和数据中心扩张带来的用电负荷增长。

5. DTE Energy $DTE
区域电力和天然气公用事业龙头，业务稳健，电网升级直接对接数据中心和工业用电增长，分红和增长兼具。

6. 第一能源 $FE
中西部主要电力公司，电网现代化投入大，能受益于AI算力对可靠电力的长期刚需。

7. CMS Energy $CMS
密歇根州核心电力和天然气供应商，业务稳定，电网升级正好匹配数据中心扩张带来的用电需求。

8. X-Energy $XE
先进小型模块化核反应堆开发商，获美国能源部支持，并与亚马逊等巨头合作，直接卡位下一代清洁可靠电力赛道。

text:
看到卫诗雅像下班一样独自回香港，就明白了梁家辉说的那句话，他说：演员只是一份职业，褪去聚光灯的光环，也不过就是普通人 。

​​卫诗雅刚拿下百花影后，没有前呼后拥的团队，没有浩浩荡荡的排场，自己推着行李走出机场。获奖是也是工作的一部分，工作结束，就安安静静回归生活。

​​在内娱，拿了大奖仿佛就要立刻被鲜花簇拥，被应酬包围。可在不少香港演员的观念里，拍戏是上班，拿奖只是这份工作里的一次嘉奖。戏散场，颁奖礼落幕，就该卸下身份回归日常。

​​周润发逛菜市场，刘青云上街买菜，梁家辉自己逛街市，被认出大多也只是点头打个招呼，不会有狂热追捧。

​卫诗雅熬了十几年，五十多部作品，大器晚成拿到影后。高光时刻很耀眼，但她没有沉浸在虚名里，领完奖就踏实返程。
​​奖项是外界给的肯定，日子终究是自己过的。演员可以被欣赏，但不必被神化。

text:
Command Code is now in Codex!!

The plan we're on is $1 a month. It comes with $10 of credits and around 15K requests.

GPT-5.6 Luna is in it, the same model we just moved to when the OpenCode sub got cut, and Grok 4.5 sits in there too next to DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and MiniMax.

Their own docs say the $1 tier has no API access. It's in our picker anyway.

So there's a dollar sub in there next to everything else now. Next time a limit hits mid loop we grab it and keep going.

quotedTweet.text:
OpenCode just got nerfed by 10x.

DeepSeek raised their prices, so the sub moved with them. 31,650 requests per 5 hours down to 3,800.

GPT-5.6 Luna now gets more usage on that same $10 sub than DeepSeek V4 Flash does, which is backwards from the whole reason most of us bought it.

So we might as well run Luna in there instead. It's the same sub and the same router, we just change which one is the default.

If you bought OpenCode Go for the DeepSeek volume then it's time to switch into Luna.

这段视频目前我还没有看到，看到的只是塌陷的评论区。其实董卿出轨这件事情的真假并不重要，重要的是今天中国大量的男性需要一个性欲的宣泄口，而董卿作为无数70后男性心目中的女神，无疑是最适合的这个宣泄对象。
疫情让大量成年男性不仅损伤了钱包，也损伤了他们的性功能，让他们既不能也不敢在异性面前跃马扬枪。但即便是太监也有对性的渴望，而中国又是一个对性资源极度封锁的国家，卖淫嫖娼的罪名让包一个小时是犯罪包一年是合法成为一个普遍现象，让今天的男性既没有钱去包一年，也没有钱去支付包一个小时的罚款，所以他们只能将自己的欲望转嫁到董卿刘亦菲这些女性身上。

text:
对冲基金大佬泰珀存储上赚了$70亿后，清仓了！开始回归七巨头：

减持
1. 美光科技 $MU  
卖出69万股，持股砍掉41%。股价狂涨242%后主动落袋为安，内存芯片周期波动大，虽然还留着大仓位，但先把超额收益锁住。

2. 闪迪 $SNDK  
全部清仓。AI存储热潮里涨幅惊人，但属于高弹性周期股，及时退出避免回调风险。

3. 康宁 $GLW  
全部清仓。光纤、玻璃材料跟AI基建沾边，但成长确定性不如核心科技巨头。

4. 拼多多 $PDD  
全部清仓。中国互联网竞争激烈，政策与消费不确定因素多。

5. 京东 $JD  
全部清仓。同样是中国电商，盈利与增长压力较大。

6. 阿里巴巴 $BABA  
大幅减持42%。中国科技股整体承压，资金转向更确定的美股巨头。

增持
7. 亚马逊 $AMZN  
加仓68万股，增持16%，成为第一大持仓。云计算AWS增速强劲、订单积压巨大，电商+云双轮驱动，现金流稳、护城河深。

8. Meta $META  
加仓23.85万股，增持55%。广告业务回暖明显，AI投入开始转化为效率和营收增长，估值相对合理。

9. 谷歌 $GOOG  
加仓11.73万股，增持约7%。搜索广告基本盘稳固，AI大模型与云业务持续发力，长期现金牛属性强。

10. 台积电 $TSM  
加仓32.25万股，增持24%。全球最先进的芯片代工厂，AI芯片几乎都要靠它生产，技术壁垒极高。

11. 优步 $UBER  
加仓约136万股，增持22%。出行与外卖业务稳健，AI应用提升效率，成长性和盈利能力双提升。

12. 英伟达 $NVDA  
小幅加仓约4%。AI算力绝对龙头，GPU需求持续旺盛，虽然仓位不算最大，但依然看好长期趋势。

存储股已经吃饱了，典型的赚了就跑，不讲武德！

所以真正该看的不是 token 单价，而是：

到了 Agent 时代，最终可能只剩一个指标有意义：

Cost per successful task。

quotedTweet.text:
On tokens and prices per token.

I said I’d write more about this, so here goes: an OpenAI token != another model’s token. We compare AI prices in dollars per million tokens as if a token were a standardized unit, like a gram or a kilowatt-hour. It isn’t. Different models use and produce the exact same text using different numbers of tokens, which means a lower price per token does not necessarily mean a lower bill.

Imagine two identical pizzas. One is cut into 8 slices at $2 each. The other is cut into 16 slices at $1.25 each. The second place advertises cheaper slices, but the whole pizza costs $20 instead of $16. Bummer ... your stomach doesn't actually care about the number of slices you just ate.

I know you are hungry now, but back to tokens. In one small comparison spanning English, technical, multilingual, and numerical text, the tokenizer we use for GPT-5.6 Sol used 766 tokens versus an estimated 1,170 for Claude Opus 5. That's a very significant difference of about 34.5% fewer tokens. You can get the same exact text, but pay for all those extra tokens. The price per token doesn't really tell this story.

Even correcting for tokenizer differences misses the bigger point. What actually matters is price per successful outcome, and for that you can use benchmarks as a starting point, but really you have to try it and measure on your own use cases.

That's all. May the tokens flow.

浙江一名少年近半年反复腹痛、胀气，人也越来越瘦，一直以为只是肠胃炎。

直到黑便持续一个多月才去医院。

癌症是中老年人的事，年轻就是免死金牌。

可身体发出的求救信号，从来不看身份证。

反复腹痛、黑便、突然消瘦，别总拿“年轻，扛一扛就好了”安慰自己。

text:
中国人评价中餐。

提问：你觉得世界上美食排名第一的国家是哪个？

中国人：当然是中国！其次法国、意大利、日本也凑合，但整体上跟中国还是差太远了，加起来只有十几个菜能吃，其他国家的美食基本都是垃圾，全世界80亿人里面，至少60亿人是大傻逼，天天只能吃狗屎，不如天天吃中餐的中国人幸福。

提问：那你觉得全中国哪里中餐的最牛逼？粤菜牛逼吗？

中国人：粤菜傻逼才吃，白切鸡、清蒸鱼一丁点味道都没有，天天吃老鼠、蛇，喝重金属中药汤喝成肾衰竭，广东人继续自己骗自己吧，一群傻逼。

提问：那你觉得鲁菜牛逼吗？

中国人：鲁菜是最垃圾的菜系，天天只有腰花、海参、丸子、酱肉，都是他妈街边菜，全是酱油葱姜蒜，山东人自己都不吃鲁菜了，天天除了超意兴把子肉就是炸鸡汉堡。

提问：那你觉得川菜牛逼吗？

中国人：川菜是典型的诈骗，放这么多辣椒就是为了掩盖食材不新鲜，四川没有新鲜的鸡鸭鱼肉，买回来都是臭的，放辣椒是为了掩盖臭味，正常人根本不能吃。

提问：那你觉得湖南江西菜牛逼吗？

中国人：这两个是最典型的穷人菜，把鸡鸭鱼肉切成小丁，往里面大量加辣椒，本质上就是为了下饭，太傻逼了，完全都是自欺欺人。

提问：那你如何评价河南菜、东北菜、北京菜、天津菜、福建菜、江浙菜、贵州菜、云南菜？

中国人：都是垃圾，根本不是人吃的，这几亿人也是纯种大傻逼，天天在饭馆吃狗屎，无药可救。

提问：那你觉得哪个地方的菜最牛逼？

中国人：我觉得中国人就讲究个锅气、烟火气，讲究个舒服，我觉得我们省我们市这边的人最懂美食。

提问：那你们省你们市有哪些代表美食？

中国人：像我们家门口的小吃一条街，还有我们这儿开了30多年的大娘炒菜，里面的大盘鸡、地锅鸡、辣椒炒肉、辣椒炒鸡、烤鱼，还有我们家后面的新疆炒拉条子、烤冷面，这些才是中国顶级美味。

你们都不懂，你们从来都没吃过，绝大多数中国人根本都不知道，一群傻逼，14亿人懂个屁美食，哪儿有我懂。

quotedTweet.text:
The copper market is facing a severe supply squeeze:

The LME’s front-month copper spread surged to a $370 per ton premium on Friday, the widest one-month spread since the 2021 supply squeeze.

This means traders are paying a historic premium for copper available in the near term versus delivery a month later, signaling that physical supply is extremely tight.

At the same time, the widely followed cash-to-three-month spread rose to $434 per ton, also the highest since 2021, prompting the LME to tighten its market controls.

This comes as LME copper stockpiles have fallen for 42 consecutive days, the longest streak since 2014, to 204,975 tons, with nearly half of the remaining metal already scheduled for withdrawal.

All while traders and producers are redirecting copper to the US, where expectations of tariffs on refined copper are pushing prices above LME levels and creating arbitrage opportunities.

The supply crunch in the copper market is far from over.

text:
本周 VIX 回到 14-15，大家可能觉得波动率没什么好说的了。但如果回头看 7 月中旬到 8 月中旬这一个月，个股端经历的不是普通的“财报后 IV crush”，而是一次极端拥挤的 dispersion 结构反向收敛。理解这件事对接下来怎么做期权至关重要。

初始条件：极端的个股高 IV / 指数低 IV 错位

7 月中旬，Cboe 的 DSPX（dispersion 指数）升到约 50%，创六年高位。与此同时 VIX 只有约 15。hyperscaler 个股 IV 约 40%，SPY 前端 IV 只有约 10%。COR1M（1 个月相关性）处于极低水平。

这个错位是怎么来的？三层溢价叠在一起：①财报风险溢价，大科技股财报集中落地前，零售开仓中 call buying 占比 56%（接近年内最高），主动买权推高事件方差；②AI 内部剧烈分化，半导体，软件，大型云各走各的，极低的股票相关性让指数 IV 没有同步上升；③7 月 momentum unwind 的尾部风险溢价，7 月科技股经历历史级别的动量平仓，单名股 realized vol 被连续大涨大跌抬高。

我们知道，指数方差 = 个股权重平方*个股方差之和 + 跨项相关系数。个股波动率很高，但隐含相关性极低，所以 VIX 可以很低。这个结构本身就是一个交易，买个股 vol、卖指数 vol、押注股票继续各走各的。这个交易在 2024-2026 年已经变得极度拥挤。

8 月初开始，四个力量同时作用于这个拥挤结构：

第一推动力：财报事件方差集中退出。 Microsoft、Google、Amazon、Meta、Apple 财报陆续落地。财报一出，事件方差几乎立刻消失。Cboe 在 8/3 就观察到 VIX 一周降 2.6 点但 VIXEQ 降 3.4 点，个股端跌得更快。但这只是触发器。普通财报季每季度都有，这次之所以这么猛，是因为财报前 DSPX 已经在六年极值。

第二推动力：拥挤的 dispersion 被反向平仓，这是最重要的放大器。 此前主流 dispersion 交易是买个股 vol / 卖指数 vol。QVR 等波动率基金甚至已经转向 reverse dispersion（买指数 vol / 卖 single-name vol），因为单名股 IV 与指数 IV 的差已经到了极端水平。财报落地后，长个股 vol 的一方同时面临：事件方差消失、theta 流失、VIXEQ/DSPX 跌破趋势、止损触发。reverse-dispersion 交易者同时在卖个股 IV。这不是自然衰减，是一轮仓位反转，这解释了为什么没有财报、或财报已经过去的股票，IV 也一起遭到压缩。市场卖的不是单个事件，是整个 single-name vol asset class。

第三推动力：7 月去杠杆结束，regime 从“怕个股爆炸”切换到“怕踏空上涨”。7 月发生历史级别科技 momentum unwind，相当一部分杠杆已被清理，去杠杆完成后市场反而具备更高质量反弹的条件。随后是典型的 underexposed chase，SPX 在截至 8/4 的四个交易日涨 5.8%，7 月 30 日至 8 月 5 日成为历史上 SPX call 成交量最高的五日窗口，短期 call skew 升至两年高位。

第四推动力：系统资金 releveraging 的负反馈循环。 截至 8/10，SOX 前十大成分股的平均 3 个月 ATM IV 仅 8 月以来就降了近 20 %。低波动率允许系统策略重新增加敞口 -> 加仓推高股价 -> 上涨进一步压低下行波动率需求 -> 更低的波动率又释放更多系统资金购买能力。这是一轮典型的 vol-control 反馈：IV 下降 -> 预期风险下降 -> 系统资金加仓 -> 股价趋势改善 -> RV 下降 -> IV 进一步下降。

这轮 crush需要让我们意识到方向正确 ≠ call 赚钱

整体 ATM IV 可以暴跌，同时远端 OTM call 仍然变贵。call demand 很强不代表你持有的 ATM 或轻度 OTM call 不会被 IV crush。Cboe 发现 8/10 前后 SPX skew 降至一年低位，但 deep OTM puts 仍有需求——这是波动率曲面的重新定价，不是所有期权都没人买。

这解释了为什么在这种环境里“方向正确”不等于“call 赚钱”。即使方向判断正确，IV 下跌带来的 Vega 损失与 Theta 损耗，仍然可能吃掉全部 Delta 收益。当 IV 变化大幅为负时，即使方向对了，总收益也可能是负的。

这轮 crush 本质上更像一次投机杠杆清洗后的波动率正常化。7 月动量股回撤、杠杆 AI 产品清算、单名股期权仓位去化之后：短期期权需求下降、散户和动量资金减少追涨、个股 realized vol 回落、Dealer 不再需要持续追着 spot 做 gamma hedge、单名股 IV 系统性下压。

现在的特殊之处在于期权结构的错位：single name stock的 ATM IV 相对便宜，但 25 Delta 和 10 Delta wings 仍然贵。 指数和个股的 term structure 都已经降到偏低区间。这对期权结构的含义很明确：想赌方向，ATM 附近的 call spread 仍然合理；想赌 IV 回归，优先买 ATM 或轻度 OTM 单腿期权吃最大 vega；不适合为了“便宜”去买很远的 wing，因为 wing skew 反而没有同步 crush。买的是被 crush 得最厉害的 ATM/轻度 OTM vol，而不是仍然昂贵的deep OTM put/call。

crush 是否已经结束？

截至 8/14：VIX 约 14.25，DSPX 约 33.45，SPY IV 处于过去一年第 4 百分位。但中位数个股 IV 仍在第 31 百分位，个股 realized volatility 仍在第 61 百分位——implied dispersion 已经下降，但 realized dispersion 尚未明显下降。IV 可能开始跑在 RV 前面。

接下来两种情景：

如果个股实际波动也逐渐下降，IV crush 还能慢慢延续。如果 realized dispersion 继续高，当前低 IV 会重新吸引买盘。此外 8/19 VIX 到期和 8/21 月度 OPEX 会移除部分压制指数波动率的 gamma 仓位，而 NVDA 财报、Jackson Hole 等事件紧接着到来。届时如果相关性开始上升，修复路径可能从“个股 IV 下跌”切换成“指数 IV 上涨”。

text:
I built a product that scares me.

It’s called RelayGraph.

I thought I was building a better way to attribute conversions when the customer journey disappears from traditional analytics.

Then I realised I was building a map of human influence.

Here’s what happens:

Person A clicks an ad then shares the link via iMessage. 

Person B clicks that link, creating the next branch, then shares it again.

Person C clicks and buys.

Normal analytics credits C as “direct.”

RelayGraph reconstructs the chain:

A → B → C → revenue

But it gets more interesting.

If A later clicks one of the links created further down the chain, RelayGraph can recognise the same browser.

The graph becomes:

A → B → C → A

A person can disappear and re-enter the same chain.

What scares me is this…

text:
David Tepper, one of the most successful and best hedge fund managers of the last 30 years, is currently shorting Berkshire Hathaway via $12.5 million in put options. 

Want to know why? Read my book. 

https://t.co/52bmKcPxH8

Here's an excerpt: 

From Chapter 10: "Float or Flotsam?"

On September 9, 2024, Ajit Jain sold 200 Class A shares of Berkshire Hathaway at an average price of $695,418 per share.

The transaction cleared roughly $139.1 million in cash. It was the largest single sale of Berkshire stock Ajit had ever made. It was also 55% of his personal stake.

Ajit Jain is the man Warren Buffett built the modern Berkshire around. He joined Berkshire in 1986. He runs the insurance operations — the National Indemnity book, the reinsurance book, the catastrophe book, the structured-settlement book, every part of the float machine that, more than any other element of the company, has produced the compounded returns Buffett is famous for. When Buffett described GEICO in his 2018 letter as having added more than $50 billion to Berkshire's intrinsic value, the man on whose desk those numbers landed was Ajit. When the Berkshire annual meeting cuts away from Buffett or Munger to a third microphone, the third microphone has been Ajit's, every year, for two decades.

In May 2025, Buffett told the Berkshire board that he was retiring. The board named Greg Abel as the next chief executive. Ajit was not promoted. 

Five days before Ajit's September sale, Berkshire's Class A shares had peaked above $727,000. Less than two weeks earlier, Berkshire's market capitalization had crossed $1 trillion for the first time in the company's history. Ajit sold five days off the all-time high.

He has continued to sell. In August 2025, 2,000 more Class B shares. In September 2025, 15,000 more Class B shares. The selling has not stopped.

Buffett, asked at the 2025 annual meeting about the sale, said nothing of substance. The financial press did not press him.

There are five operating buckets at Berkshire Hathaway. Insurance, the equity portfolio, the railroad, the power company, and the sprawling industrial-and-consumer subsidiary book Berkshire calls Manufacturing, Service, and Retailing (MSR). Four of the five are broken. The railroad, as we've documented, is failing. The power company is at risk to being wiped out by lawsuits and, perhaps even more importantly, by a generational shift away from renewables. Most of the MSR revenues are low margin and aren't growing.

But it is insurance that has always been (and should always be) the heart of Berkshire. If the float grows, so will the share price. If the float grows, the problems at the railroad can be fixed. If the float grows, the power company's losses can be managed. If the float grows, the portfolio can be improved.

But if the float doesn't grow, Berkshire is in serious trouble.

Yes, Berkshire has an enormous cash hoard — $373 billion at year-end 2025, the largest non-financial cash position in the history of corporate America. I'm not suggesting that Berkshire is going to collapse. What I am saying, and what this book is really all about, is what Berkshire must do right now to take back its rightful place as America's very best company.

Ajit doesn't believe those changes are going to happen. Or else he wouldn't be selling. And that, above everything else in this book, should make the board pay attention.

Berkshire's biggest problem hasn't happened yet. But it is about to.

* * *

Greg Abel's inaugural shareholder letter, in February 2026, said GEICO's rate increases had restored margins but cost the company customers. He said competitors' rate reductions might extend that pressure into 2026. He said restoring retention while maintaining underwriting discipline would take time.

What Abel did not say, but is true: the pricing-cycle that allowed Progressive and GEICO to raise rates aggressively in 2022 through 2024 has now turned. The hard market is over. The soft market is here. Moody's projects that twelve of the top sixteen American property-and-casualty insurers will see combined-ratio deterioration in 2026. Industry-wide premium growth in personal auto will fall from 9% in 2024 to roughly 4% in 2026.

Soft markets reward the carriers who entered them with the better risk-segmentation engine. They punish the carriers who entered with a weaker one. Progressive enters the 2026 soft market with 33 million policies and the most-mature usage-based-insurance platform in the industry. GEICO enters with a shrunken book, a new chief executive in her first year, and a telematics product that Ajit himself, in May 2025, claimed was now "as good as anyone" — a claim no analyst has been able to verify, and which is contradicted by the customer-acquisition numbers.

Berkshire's insurance premium float, which generated $176 billion of investable capital at year-end 2025, may not grow at all in the next five years. The two-point-2% underwriting profit on float that Ajit disclosed at the 2024 meeting will not repeat in a soft cycle. The cost of float, which has been below the Treasury-bill rate in 63% of measured years over Berkshire's history, will rise.

Insurance is the engine. The engine is sputtering. And Ajit Jain is selling.

Insurance, the equity portfolio, the railroad, the power company, and the sprawling industrial-and-consumer subsidiary book Berkshire calls Manufacturing, Service, and Retailing (MSR). Four of the five are broken. The railroad, as we've documented, is failing. The power company is at risk to being wiped out by lawsuits and, perhaps even more importantly, by a generational shift away from renewables. Most of the MSR revenues are low margin and aren't growing.

But it is insurance that has always been (and should always be) the heart of Berkshire. If the float grows, so will the share price. If the float grows, the problems at the railroad can be fixed. If the float grows, the power company's losses can be managed. If the float grows, the portfolio can be improved.

But if the float doesn't grow, Berkshire is in serious trouble.

Yes, Berkshire has an enormous cash hoard — $373 billion at year-end 2025, the largest non-financial cash position in the history of corporate America. I'm not suggesting that Berkshire is going to collapse. What I am saying, and what this book is really all about, is what Berkshire must do right now to take back its rightful place as America's very best company.

Ajit doesn't believe those changes are going to happen. Or else he wouldn't be selling. And that, above everything else in this book, should make the board pay attention.

Berkshire's biggest problem hasn't happened yet. But it is about to.

* * *

Greg Abel's inaugural shareholder letter, in February 2026, said GEICO's rate increases had restored margins but cost the company customers. He said competitors' rate reductions might extend that pressure into 2026. He said restoring retention while maintaining underwriting discipline would take time.

What Abel did not say, but is true: the pricing-cycle that allowed Progressive and GEICO to raise rates aggressively in 2022 through 2024 has now turned. The hard market is over. The soft market is here. Moody's projects that twelve of the top sixteen American property-and-casualty insurers will see combined-ratio deterioration in 2026. Industry-wide premium growth in personal auto will fall from 9% in 2024 to roughly 4% in 2026.

Soft markets reward the carriers who entered them with the better risk-segmentation engine. They punish the carriers who entered with a weaker one. Progressive enters the 2026 soft market with 33 million policies and the most-mature usage-based-insurance platform in the industry. GEICO enters with a shrunken book, a new chief executive in her first year, and a telematics product that Ajit himself, in May 2025, claimed was now "as good as anyone" — a claim no analyst has been able to verify, and which is contradicted by the customer-acquisition numbers.

Berkshire's insurance premium float, which generated $176 billion of investable capital at year-end 2025, may not grow at all in the next five years. The two-point-2% underwriting profit on float that Ajit disclosed at the 2024 meeting will not repeat in a soft cycle. The cost of float, which has been below the Treasury-bill rate in 63% of measured years over Berkshire's history, will rise.

Insurance is the engine. The engine is sputtering. And Ajit Jain is selling.

text:
VMware vCenter CVE-2026-59310 has moved well beyond “patch this critical RCE.”

New incident-response findings link exploitation to ~361 victim IPs across 47 countries and show the full chain:

→ pre-auth/root execution on VCSA
→ cron + systemd persistence
→ vmdir credential theft
→ new privileged vSphere accounts
→ ESXi access
→ Babuk-derived ransomware
The key defensive point: vCenter is the control plane. If exploitation occurred, patching alone doesn’t remove identities, SSH access, web shells or persistence already planted.
Attribution to a China-nexus actor is currently moderate-confidence, not definitive.

QUIRSO — original incident research:
 https://t.co/bTwr0Vu0zI
Primary source for the 361 victim IPs / 47 countries and observed exploitation campaign.

Broadcom — VMSA-2026-0006 / official advisory:
 https://t.co/yFOKwadjuu
Authoritative source for CVE-2026-59310, CVSS 9.8, affected products and patches.

The Hacker News — Aug. 17 follow-up with ransomware/attribution details:
 https://t.co/v4P1rnbX7k
Covers QUIRSO's moderate-confidence China-nexus assessment and the expanded post-exploitation/ransomware findings.

Shadowserver — victim notification/special report:
 https://t.co/XpzJfVrcn2
Shadowserver says the systems supplied by QUIRSO should be considered fully compromised, specifically noting the reverse_ssh persistence mechanism.

https://t.co/VaLIDTiydD — official CVE record:
 https://t.co/SfwzqNDa0F

text:
Me and my good friend Fable 5 finished a search for a 1967 number theory problem and man was it a trip.

Lander–Parkin–Selfridge, sixth powers, three vs two:

x⁶ + y⁶ + z⁶ = a⁶ + b⁶

No solutions with every base below 150,000. 4 days 20 hours, 3,081 CPU-hours, ~$5 of electricity, 0 failures under re-verification. 354x past the last explicit search (Ekl 1998), 4.5x past anything implied since, and the first explicit search of the −1 near-miss residual. All five known +1 identities came back. No −1 below 30,000.

!!!!Bonus find: there is a reason every near miss ends in +1. Mod 7, 8, 9 the equation just counts coprime bases, generic value 3−2 = +1. A −1 miss needs two extra divisibility coincidences, roughly 85:1 against. The desert is arithmetic, not luck.!!!!

C++ / OpenMP, CUDA behind a gate. Every candidate re-derived on CPU in 128-bit, then checked again in Python.

https://t.co/I3NBfpxdLC

If you work on Euler / LPS / power sums, break the run or the claim. Clone it, build it, ./lps632 selftest rediscovers all five identities from scratch.

No solutions with every base below 150,000. 4 days 20 hours, 3,081 CPU-hours, ~$5 of electricity, 0 failures under re-verification. 354x past the last explicit search (Ekl 1998), 4.5x past anything implied since, and the first explicit search of the −1 near-miss residual. All five known +1 identities came back. No −1 below 30,000.

!!!!Bonus find: there is a reason every near miss ends in +1. Mod 7, 8, 9 the equation just counts coprime bases, generic value 3−2 = +1. A −1 miss needs two extra divisibility coincidences, roughly 85:1 against. The desert is arithmetic, not luck.!!!!

C++ / OpenMP, CUDA behind a gate. Every candidate re-derived on CPU in 128-bit, then checked again in Python.

https://t.co/I3NBfpxdLC

If you work on Euler / LPS / power sums, break the run or the claim. Clone it, build it, ./lps632 selftest rediscovers all five identities from scratch.

Growing up, I always wanted to build "something cool." After leaving Florida, I didn't really know what that would look like. 

I'm genuinely excited to say we're officially building that cool thing at Sandberg Phoenix with @AlgorithmTalent. 

Working with athletes, coaches, ADs, and GMs over the past four years has been what I love, and now I'm going all in on that. 

Our goal is to represent the best people, who just happen to also be incredible athletes, Coaches, and GMs. 

Am I nervous and anxious? Yes. 

Are we fully prepared for the grind, heck yes. So if you're an athlete looking for representation in high school or college, feel free to reach out anytime. 

The long term vision is to bring a team together that will be able to represent you far into the future as well, with the next 12-18 months putting a team in place with NFL, NBA, WNBA, and more certifications. 

The reward for good work, is more work, and today is day 1. Lets get to work.

result.text:
Growing up, I always wanted to build "something cool." After leaving Florida, I didn't really know what that would look like. 

I'm genuinely excited to say we're officially building that cool thing at Sandberg Phoenix with @AlgorithmTalent. 

Working with athletes, coaches, ADs, and GMs over the past four years has been what I love, and now I'm going all in on that. 

Our goal is to represent the best people, who just happen to also be incredible athletes, Coaches, and GMs. 

Am I nervous and anxious? Yes. 

Are we fully prepared for the grind, heck yes. So if you're an athlete looking for representation in high school or college, feel free to reach out anytime. 

The long term vision is to bring a team together that will be able to represent you far into the future as well, with the next 12-18 months putting a team in place with NFL, NBA, WNBA, and more certifications. 

The reward for good work, is more work, and today is day 1. Lets get to work.
